48.dek: More trucks came looking for work. Less freight needed moving. Prices went up anyway. That's the holiday doing what holidays do, landing on top of a cost floor that isn't going anywhere.
48.alt: Night photo: crowded truck stop, one truck pulling out

47.dek: Contract van rates hit $3.28/mi in October, matching the May 2022 record, while freight volume actually fell.
47.alt: A semi truck on a snowy highway at night

46.dek: Nine months of spot-above-contract ended this week. Spot linehaul printed $2.50 against a contract average of $2.73, a 23¢ spread in your favor, widening toward DAT's $2.23 call. Carriers lock 2027 pricing in three to four weeks.
46.alt: A highway curving into the dusk

45.dek: The price to move a truckload of goods is drifting down, just like the forecasters said it would. It's still way above last year, but for the first time in months, the trend is on your side.
45.alt: Two trucks side by side on a highway at night

43.dek: USDOT put $200M into 14 truck parking projects on October 14, the second federal supply-side intervention of 2026 after Freedom Haulers.
43.alt: Trailers parked in rows at a truck terminal at dusk

42.dek: Holiday food and CPG freight starts staging in mid-October, and reefer rejections historically run 1.5–2x dry van into the holiday. This year the turn lands on a 10.93 load-to-truck base.
42.alt: Night photo: reefer leaving a cold-storage dock, mist

41.dek: Dry van hit $2.28/mi and rejections firmed to 12.6% heading into Q4. Some models call it quarter-end noise that fades by November.
41.alt: Night photo: fall-colour hills, winding road from above

40.dek: DAT says the tightening is capacity exits, not demand. Van found its floor at $2.21. And Port Tracker's first 2027 print shows January imports holding at 2.09M TEU.
40.alt: Night photo: nearly empty trucking yard, truck leaving

39.dek: OTRI pulled back to 13.22% and tender volumes dropped 10%, yet spot rates resumed climbing after Labor Day. Capacity is exiting as fast as demand is softening.
39.alt: Night photo: highway fork from straight above

38.dek: OTRI printed 12.9%, the first week-over-week rise since the July peak broke, and van rates have flattened to a penny-a-week crawl. One uptick is a warning; two is a closed window.
38.alt: Night photo: long uphill grade seen across a valley

36.dek: CVSA Brake Safety Week wrapped August 29. Historically ~1 in 7 inspected trucks goes out of service, and this week they re-enter in a lump, right into a Labor Day short week. The board will look looser. It isn't.
36.alt: Night photo: trucks merging back from a rest area, pines

35.dek: CVSA Brake Safety Week runs Aug 24–29 against a 10.93 load-to-truck backdrop. Meanwhile FMCSA flips on its new Motus registry, imports crest at 2.22M TEU, and spot slides across all three equipment types.
35.alt: Night photo: trucks queued at a roadside inspection

34.dek: Dry van spot fell nearly 6 cents in a single week, the largest decline in the data set. Section 301 tariffs now touch 99% of imports with USEC ocean at a record $9,144/FEU. Werner grew revenue 24% and still cut fleet guidance.
34.alt: Night photo: steep pass, switchbacks dropping away

33.dek: On July 30, President Trump and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy hosted veterans at the White House to launch the Freedom Haulers campaign, an expedited CDL licensing pathway for military veterans with heavy-vehicle experience.
33.alt: Night photo: one truck on an empty plain, Milky Way

32.dek: The $604 million Dallas County verdict against CH Robinson is advisory and will be appealed, a process that could run four to five years. But the industry is not waiting for the appeal to conclude.
32.alt: Night photo: truck passing a courthouse downtown

31.dek: On July 23, a Dallas County jury awarded $604 million in compensatory damages in a case involving a fatal 2021 crash in Jackson, Mississippi.
31.alt: Night photo: under a freeway stack interchange

30.dek: JB Hunt reported second-quarter earnings on July 15 and the results were unambiguous: revenue up 19% year-over-year, EPS up 45%, intermodal volume up 10%, the first double-digit volume growth in a decade.
30.alt: Night photo: four-way crossroads from straight above

29.dek: Flatbed crossed $3.00 per mile last week, a milestone that has never been reached before.
29.alt: Night photo: flatbed with steel beside a steel mill

28.dek: Since the week of May 4, inbound reefer rates into the 11 World Cup host city markets have risen +11.4%, from $4.11/mi to $4.58/mi. Over the same period, rates into all other US markets rose just 6%, and then reversed.
28.alt: Night photo: stadium glowing beside the highway

27.dek: For the first time since 2021, spot truckload rates have caught and in some lanes exceeded contract rates.
27.alt: Night photo: fireworks over a river town

26.dek: The rate environment you've been navigating since February has a structural explanation that goes beyond spot cycles and seasonal patterns.
26.alt: Night photo: row of dark parked trucks, one lit

25.dek: The freight community woke Sunday to the most consequential geopolitical shift of 2026: a framework agreement between the United States and Iran that includes a 60-day ceasefire and the full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping.
25.alt: Night photo: refinery at night beside the road

24.dek: Three editions ago, we called the structural shift: not a seasonal bounce, but a genuine repricing driven by capacity exits.
24.alt: Night photo: intermodal rail yard from an overpass

23.dek: The national average on-highway diesel came in at $5.523/gal for the week of May 25, a 7-cent drop week-over-week, the third consecutive weekly decline. But the structural picture hasn't changed.
23.alt: Night photo: steel truss bridge over a river

22.dek: The national average on-highway diesel came in at $5.596/gal for the week of May 18, a modest 4-cent drop week-over-week, but don't let that fool you.
22.alt: Night photo: lakeside road, docks and cabins

21.dek: The national average for on-highway diesel held at $5.64/gal this week, essentially flat week-over-week, but that number requires context.
21.alt: Night photo: first light of dawn, straight highway east

20.dek: The national average for on-highway diesel surged to $5.64/gal as of May 4, up $0.29 from the prior week, a 5.4% single-week increase. This is not a temporary spike. Fuel costs are now $2.13/gal higher year-over-year (+61%).
20.alt: Night photo: weigh station scale lane

19.dek: The national average for on-highway diesel fell to $5.35/gal as of April 27, down $0.05 from the prior week. While this marks the third consecutive week of declines from the mid-April peak, it is not a structural shift.

18.dek: The national average for on-highway diesel fell to $5.40/gal as of April 20, down $0.21 from the prior week.
18.alt: Night photo: truck entering a mountain tunnel

17.dek: Fifty days into the Iran conflict, the energy shock that began with the closure of the Strait of Hormuz on March 4 is not fading, it is intensifying.
17.alt: Night photo: fuel island at a truck stop
